text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 12 in history:
1667 - The first successful blood transfusion was carried out by Jean-Baptiste Denys, personal physician to King Louis XIV of France, on a 15-year-old-boy using blood from a sheep.
1759 - William Collins, considered one of the finest English lyric poets of the 18th century, died.
1819 - Charles Kingsley, British clergyman and writer, born. Also an Anglican clergyman, he is famous for his anti-Catholic adventure story "Westward Ho!" and his children's book "The Water Babies".
1839 - Cooperstown, New York, was chosen as the site of the National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum after Abner Doubleday had formulated the rules of baseball there.
1842 - Thomas Arnold, English educator who reformed the public school system in England, died.
1897 - Sir Anthony Eden, British Conservative prime minister 1955-7, born; he was forced out of office by ill health and controversy over his Suez policy.
1898 - During the Spanish-American War, the independence of the Philippines was declared by Gen. Emilio Aguinaldo, leader of the revolutionary movement, with the support of the U.S.
1924 - George Bush, 41st president of the United States 1989-93, born.

1929 - Anne Frank, Jewish wartime diarist, born in Germany. Her diary has captivated millions with her account of growing up in occupied Amsterdam during World War Two. She died in Bergen-Belsen concentration camp in March 1945.
1935 - A truce ended the Chaco War, a conflict fought between Bolivia and Paraguay during 1932-35.
1944 - Chinese Communist leader Mao Zedong announced that he would support Nationalist leader Chiang Kai-shek in the war against Japan.
1957 - Jimmy Dorsey, U.S. band leader and saxophonist, died.
1971 - In Malta, Dom Mintoff defeated Borg Olivier by one seat in a general election.
1975 - Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was found guilty of corrupt election practices in 1971, but refused to resign.

1978 - "Son of Sam" multiple killer David Berkowitz, who went on a murder rampage that terrorised New York City, received the maximim penalty -- 25 years to life in prison -- with a recommendation that he spend the rest of his days in prison.
1981 - In Poland, Prime Minister Wojciech Jaruzelski sacked five cabinet ministers and proposed a major reconstruction of the government to tackle a severe economic crisis.
1982 - Dame Marie Rambert, Polish-born founder of the Ballet Rambert, died.
1990 - The parliament of the Russian Federation formally declared its sovereignty.

1991 - Mount Pinatubo, a Philippine volcano, erupted for a third time just 14 hours after unleashing a series of explosions that shut down the biggest U.S. air base in Asia. The volcano had been dormant for six centuries.
1991 - Bangladesh's former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad was sentenced to 10 years imprisonment for illegal possession of firearms.
1991 - Radical Boris Yeltsin defeated orthodox Communist rivals in the first direct elections to the presidency of the powerful Russian republic.
1993 - Nigerians voted for a civilian president after a decade of army rule.
1994 - Haiti's military-backed provisional president declared a state of emergency, saying the country faced "extreme danger" and possible "invasion and occupation".
1994 - Menachem Schneerson, the head of the ultra-Orthodox Lubavitch movement and a figure of great religious power in Judaism, died in New York.
1995 - Italian Arturo Benedetti Michelangeli, hailed as one of the greatest pianists of the 20th century, died.
